questions.q: How big is a black hole's dark shadow compared with its event horizon?
questions.do: Look at the readouts beside the ray-traced picture at the top. Read Shadow edge (photon capture) and Photon sphere.
questions.a: The shadow edge is 2.60 rs, about 2.6 times the horizon radius. Light can orbit at the photon sphere, 1.5 rs, and the disk starts at 3 rs.

questions.q: A 1 g ship flies to Gaia BH1 and to M87*. How long does each trip take for the crew, and for people at home?
questions.do: In The black holes we know, click the Gaia BH1 row and read Getting there at 1 g under the charts. Then click the M87* row.
questions.a: Gaia BH1: 14.3 years aboard, about 1,562 years at home. M87*: 34.6 years aboard, but 55.0 million years at home. The table's 1 g ship, crew years column shows the same crew times.

questions.q: Once inside the horizon, how long could you last at Sagittarius A* compared with M87*?
questions.do: Click the Sagittarius A* row and read Longest you can survive inside the horizon. Then click the M87* row.
questions.a: Sagittarius A*: about 66.5 s. M87*: about 27.9 hours. M87* is about 1,500 times heavier, so its horizon is bigger and the fall to the centre takes longer.

questions.q: Why would you be torn apart long before reaching Gaia BH1, but cross M87*'s horizon without feeling anything?
questions.do: Click Gaia BH1 and read A person is torn apart (10 g stretch) at and the verdict. Do the same for M87*.
questions.a: At Gaia BH1 the stretch reaches 10 g about 3,605 km from the centre, about 127 horizon radii out, because its horizon is only 28 km. M87*'s horizon is 128 AU, so you reach it while still far from the centre, where the tides are gentle. The verdict says You would cross the horizon intact.

questions.q: Who first showed that general relativity allows a bridge (wormhole), and who later asked what a travellable one would need?
questions.do: Read the text in Wormholes: allowed on paper, never seen. Then look at Negative energy needed for the starting Throat radius of 1.0 m.
questions.a: Einstein and Rosen found the bridge in 1935, but it pinches shut faster than light can cross it. In 1988 Michael Morris and Kip Thorne showed that a travellable throat needs matter with negative energy density. Even a 1 m throat needs about 0.71 Jupiter masses of it. No wormhole has ever been observed.
